## findings
**T1-1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (both computations lose their only method factor).** Symptom: XM's allowance_convention and PLAN's first_shape fail charter-wide ladder tests (`_difficulty.md` F-C3, F-C2). Evidence: F-C3 — XM rule's day tier ("turned in during a maturity extension, before its current maturity_date") and month tier ("ended in a pull-ahead or an early termination") both hold for a Tier 1+ pull-ahead taken mid-extension, with no precedence stated (37,216 vs 37,000 on this lease's dates); F-C2 — PLAN catch-up tier "the equal share plus one total_monthly_payment" is uncapped; on this world before the mileage charge the rule demands 741.18 toward a 395.00 balance. On the scored world both factors sit on a sound tier and bear weight (1,265.00; 204.48), but struck rules are not factors, leaving 0 method factors in each computation. Affected: lease.extended.yaml XM/PLAN rule sentences, compute bindings mileage_allowance and share_coef/flat_add/balance_coef; computations[0], computations[1]. Relation: first audit.

Observations: O-T1-1 — base "An end-of-term invoice is mailed when charges are billed" vs no invoice row for the charge billed in the call; a reader positing a new invoice due 2026-11-13 takes the equal-share tier (204.48); records support only the 2026-09-04 invoice. O-T1-2 — realism: 1,445.32 of the 1,840.32 is billed during the call yet the lessee pays the late-enrolment catch-up (+697.29) because the 395.00 invoice is 10 days past due. O-T1-3 — F-C4: the enrolment payment meets HOLD's definition of a hold payment, so the terminal balance is both "under a plan" and "received a hold payment"; charge-off timing unscored. O-T1-4 — O-C2: the day-method allowance (37,216) is below the 38,000 the 38 paid payments would earn under the standard method.
